LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: POETRY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.5 Guided Writing: Mechanics of Writing (2 Sessions) • Punctuation mark
Topic 3.6: Guided writing: Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided writing: Poetry, part of Writing 3.5 Guided Writing: Mechanics of Writing (2 Sessions) • Punctuation mark in Grade 8 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How do we keep our utensils clean? 2. Why should we writie poems?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. team up to create a vocabulary bank with words related to the theme,

2. complete sentences using appropriate vocabulary on kitchen items and meals,

3. work jointly with peers to rearrange jumbled up sentences to make coherent and logic paragraphs,

4. derive words from the vocabulary list based on the theme to compose a simple poem,

5. collaborate with peers to memorise and recite the poem in class or during clubs and societies. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. team up to create a vocabulary bank with words related to the theme,
2. complete sentences using appropriate vocabulary on kitchen items and meals,
3. work jointly with peers to rearrange jumbled up sentences to make coherent and logic paragraphs,
4. derive words from the vocabulary list based on the theme to compose a simple poem,
5. collaborate with peers to memorise and recite the poem in class or during clubs and societies. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided writing: Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and Problem solving: These are promoted as the learner follows simple instructions to rearrange jumbled up

sentences to make coherent and logic paragraphs.

• Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner exchanges new ideas that inspire creativity when memorising and

reciting the poem in class or during clubs and societies.

Values:
Unity: This is promoted as the learner teams up to create a vocabulary bank with words related to the theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Lifestyle: This is addressed as the learner recognises and appreciates different ways of preparing meals for a healthy lifestyle.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of poetry and its performance to their learning in Creative Arts and Sports.
